newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity moves higher on weather, supply.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity moves higher on weather, supply.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading higher Monday, continuing to find strength on cooling demand in the Southwest and power supply constraints in the Northwest, industry sources said.
As of 1210 EDT, May Palo Verde was up 25 cents at the day's high of $17.75 after trade as low as $17.50, while June PV was up 13 cents at $18.70 per megawatt hour (MWh).

May California Oregon Border (COB) was trading up seven cents at the day's high of $14.10 after morning exchanges as low as $13.50 per MWh, while June COB was steady from Friday's settlement at $13.45 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1140 an estimated total of 43 COB and 109 PV contracts had traded.
Forecasts called for at least two more days of above-normal temperatures in the Southwest, giving strength to cash prices and psychological support to futures, the industry sources said.
Spot power availability in the West has also been lowered by a number of plant outages at various generation stations.
The 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon nuclear unit 1, in Avila Beach, California, was idled Saturday as planned for a 36-day refueling and maintenance outage.
The 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 nuclear power unit remained out of service for refueling, with an expected restart date in late June.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear plant in Washington state was also shut for refueling, and was expected to resume power output in early July.
Hydroelectric output in Northwest has been running relatively low in recent weeks due to a slower-than-normal snowmelt and spillage on the Snake and Columbia Rivers.

About 6,000 MW of thermal generating capacity was off-line in the West for planned and unplanned maintenance, as well as hydropower displacement sales, but some of the capacity is expected to return to service later this week.
Forecasts called for temperatures in the Southwest to run six to 12 degrees Fahrenheit above normal through Tuesday, and moderate to near normal levels for the rest of the week.
Temperatures in the Northwest were forecast to be three to six degrees above normal through Tuesday with chance of rain. Temperaturees were then expected to cool to near normal levels through Friday.
